content:
I'm working on a project that involves a large amount of proofs involving BitVecs, and I'm finding them absolutely miserable to work with. Trivial goals can't be closed by bv_decide or omega since they just throw their hands up whenever they hit a modulo or 2^n, and a lot of basic theorems are missing.
If anyone has any helpful tips or tricks for how to make working with BitVecs less awful, I'd greatly appreciate it.

Just to give an example of the type of issues I keep running into, what finally prompted this post was spending way too much time on proving the following goal:
n : Nat byte1 : BitVec n byte2 : BitVec n h : BitVec.toNat (byte1 - byte2) = 0 ⊢ byte1 = byte2
As you can probably understand, needing to spend time and effort to prove things like this is not exactly pleasant.

First things first, bv_decide does not aim to solve formulas like this, it is a decision procedure for fixed width bv where the n is a numeral not an abstract value. I also don't think a lot of theorems are missing here, for one you can trivially find a proof by grind:

import Lean.LibrarySuggestions.Default

example (w : Nat) (x y : BitVec w) (h : BitVec.toNat (x - y) = 0) : x = y := by
  grind +suggestions

alternatively you could've also done:

example (w : Nat) (x y : BitVec w) (h : BitVec.toNat (x - y) = 0) : x = y := by
  apply BitVec.eq_of_toNat_eq
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge x.toNat y.toNat with h2 | h2
  · rw [BitVec.toNat_sub_of_lt h2] at h
    omega
  · rw [BitVec.toNat_sub_of_le h2] at h
    omega

or something similar (this is also basically the proof that grind ends up identifying here). I'd say the important tricks for figuring out small technicalities like this are to know how to use tools like https://loogle.lean-lang.org, grind, simp, aesop if you are in mathlib

Ah, i see. If I'm using Mathlib's BitVec, grind +suggestions fails, but with the vanilla BitVec, it doesn't. As for the other tactics you mentioned, aesop and simp both also failed on this.

The missing theorems i was thinking about are mostly ones that have equivalent theorems for Nat and also apply to BitVec, but for some reason aren't available for BitVec directly. Using them is quite annoying as converting to Nat introduces a bunch of 2^n and modulo terms which one has to then manually get rid of, which is often more work than just proving the goal without using said theorem.

What do you mean by mathlibs BitVec? There should only be oelne BitVec type. Im also aware that the other tactics I mentioned won't get it one shot but they can get you a good chunk if the way there. The most important point here was probably how to use loogle.

Note also that if your hypothesis was x - y = 0 instead of the toNat version, deriving x = y would be a lot easier, and just be solvable with BitVec.sub_eq_iff_eq_add. The issus is that you are converting toNat which forces you to think about more stuff. Furthermore, as you can see above there is also no need to manually get rid of the modulo in a lot of cases. The main question you need to ask yourself for these theorems is how to use the ~100 lemmas about toNat to your advantage as opposed to redoing the fundamental work over and over again.

By Mathlib's BitVec i mean if i import Mathlib.Data.BitVec then grind +suggestions fails.

I'm definitely trying to get better at using loogle. That last part of what you said is essentially what i was trying to ask help with, but clearly didn't know how to phrase very well. Sorry about the miscommunication, that's entirely on me.
To debug this, you could locally make a copy of mathlib's BitVec.lean, add your failing test at the end, and then delete one command at a time from just above your test until it passes

Did you manage to work around the 2 ^ n thing? I'm consistently hitting those cases and grind can't proceed, many lemmas are not through if I don't have n > 0, but even with that does not work. If i fix a width, grind works just fine.
